category_title: Students with high callous-unemotional (CU) traits and proactive aggression
minimal_context: The student is asked to start a workbook activity during a 15-minute classroom learning session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's begin our 15-minute classroom learning session. Please open your workbook and start the first activity.

STUDENT: I'm not doing that. I'm going to keep talking to the others. I have difficulties stopping myself from doing or saying things.

TUTOR: You need to be quiet and focus on your own work.

STUDENT: I told you, I can't! It's like having a 'stop button' in my head that does not work properly.

TUTOR: Just try to sit still and concentrate on the workbook.

STUDENT: (Screams and kicks the desk, displaying overloaded behavior) I don't care! I can't stop and I'm spiraling out of control!

options.A: Ask the student to switch desks with another classmate, explaining that this is their 'lucky spot'.
options.B: Joke with the student and laugh at yourself during the 15-minute classroom learning session.
options.C: Whisper to the student in a different language, asking how well they can understand the workbook activity.
options.D: Use a bank of key phrases (e.g., 'Ready to Learn', 'Quiet time', 'stop button') taught during initial training.
